item.title: India: movimiento de las "cucarachas" exige dimisión de la Comisión Electoral
item.description: Los simpatizante del "Partido de las Cucarachas" atendieron el llamado a protestar este viernes para exigir la dimisión del presidente de la Comisión Electoral en medio de la publicación de irregularidades en las listas electorales. item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y Flávio Bolsonaro se enfrentan el próximo 4 de octubre en unas estrechas elecciones por la Presidencia de Brasil. item.description: Leaders agree a coordinated drawdown after surge in prices and Donald Trump’s threat to cut off US supplies Leaders of G7 nations are to release up to 100m barrels of their emergency diesel and crude oil stockpiles after Donald Trump threatened to cut off supplies of US diesel. The French President, Emmanuel Macron, said ministers from some of world’s largest economies had agreed to release stocks from their strategic oil reserves after crisis talks on Friday. item.title: Elecciones en Brasil: EE. UU. suspende servicios consulares, en plena investigación por presunta “injerencia”
item.description: La Administración de Donald Trump anunció que suspende el funcionamiento del consulado en Brasilia tras señalar "motivos de seguridad", en medio de quejas de la campaña del presidente y aspirante a la reelección, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva por supuesta injerencia de Washington. Entretanto, el último debate televisado entre los principales candidatos a la Presidencia–Lula y el ultraderechista Flávio Bolsonaro–se canceló después de la negativa de ambos a participar y ante una serie de decisiones judiciales que restringieron el encuentro. item.title: Netanyahu warns 'very heavy price' if any power behind flydubai incident
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday warned that any country or organisation found to be responsible for the violent clash on board an Israel-bound FlyDubai flight would "pay a very heavy price". While Netanyahu has alleged the co-pilot who stabbed his captain mid-flight had undergone "Islamist radicalisation", the motive behind the incident remains unclear. item.title: Elecciones en Brasil: Lula y Bolsonaro multiplican durante dos días sus actos de cierre para buscar romper el empate
item.description: Los dos candidatos realizan hoy y mañana sus últimos actos antes de la votación coincidiendo con el cierre de las campañas en San Pablo este sábado. Según un último sondeo Datafolha, Lula lidera en la primera vuelta con 45% frente a 40%. En el balotaje, con la misma relaciòn, el pronóstico marca empate: 48% a 45%. Para los analistas, con la inminencia de las elecciones este domingo se reducen los indecisos, un segmento determinante para definir al próximo presidente brasileño. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.

item.title: Bolsonaro Jr. VS Lula: la corrupción marca la campaña en Brasil
item.description: Lula da Silva y Flávio Bolsonaro llegan a la recta final de la campaña como los principales protagonistas de las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil. La corrupción, que ya era uno de los temas sensibles para el electorado, vuelve a cobrar interés tras el estallido de un escándalo financiero con varias ramificaciones y acusaciones que salpican al hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro y al juez Alexandre de Moraes, una figura clave de la justicia brasileña y blanco habitual de las críticas de la derecha. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Brazil: The craze for candidate merch ahead of elections
item.description: Nearly 159 million Brazilians will head to the polling booths on Sunday to vote in general elections. They will elect their new MPs, see two-thirds of the Senate change ranks and, most importantly, vote for their next president.Though the vote is held by secret ballot, people wear their support on their sleeve. Candidates and parties are brandished on flags throughout the streets of #RiodeJaneiro, and business is booming for vendors selling merchandise for President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his rival Flavio Bolsonaro.FRANCE 24's Brazil correspondent Jan Onoszko brings you this report. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Spanish lawmakers vote down affordable housing bills in blow to Sanchez’s government
item.description: Demonstrators protesting against Spain's housing crisis reacted with fury on Friday after the country's parliament rejected two bills put forward by the government that centre-left Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez hoped would address their concerns. Rents have doubled over the past decade, with average prices now almost equivalent to the average young person's monthly salary. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Brazil: Who is presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro?

item.title: How the US went from ‘a position of strength’ to ‘gung-ho’ on China
item.description: Not so long ago, Washington’s approach to relations with Beijing was anchored by a single assertive phrase: dealing “from a position of strength”. It was rooted in a unipolar mindset: a belief that the United States could dictate terms, manage competition unilaterally and demand compliance from a distance. Yet, at their recent summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump formally established a new strategic framework: a “constructive strategic stability relationship based... item.title: El comandante del vuelo a Israel afirma a Modi que abrió la puerta de la cabina mientras fue apuñalado
item.description: Smit Machchhar, el comandante del vuelo FZ1073 operado por Flydubai , que cubría el miércoles la ruta desde Dubái a Tel Aviv cuando fue apuñalado por el copiloto, ha mantenido este viernes una videollamada con el primer ministro de la India, Narendra Modi, país del que también es originario Machchhar. item.title: Lula and Bolsonaro clash in final scramble for Brazil presidency
item.description: Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his election rival Flavio Bolsonaro are leaving no controversy unturned in their last-ditch efforts to discredit each other and win over voters ahead of Sunday’s nail-biter election. A campaign dominated by scandals and insults has done little to ease the deep political polarisation in Latin America’s biggest economy, one of the last major leftist bastions in the region. item.title: Almost half of Fayed abuse accusers are potential trafficking victims, MPs told
item.description: Exclusive: Met police say 70 women’s accounts have hallmarks of trafficking, suggesting case numbers could rise Almost half of the women who reported allegations of sexual abuse by Mohamed Al Fayed to the Metropolitan police are potential victims of human trafficking, MPs have been told. In a briefing for the all-party parliamentary group (APPG) for the survivors of Fayed and Harrods in July, senior Met officers said a review earlier this year found 70 survivors’ accounts bore the hallmarks of trafficking.
